title: Genome resequencing and identification of variations by Illumina Genome Analyzer Reads
protocol: Concatenate chromosome sequences from NCBI build v36 reference assembly into a single FASTA format file.
Align Illumina GA reads to the reference sequence using SOAP1 software with the command line parameter "-c 52" for trimming low-quality bases.
For single-end data, use the following command: soap -a <Reads.fastq> -d <Reference.fasta> -o <Alignment.soap> -p <# of parallel processes> -c 52 -s 12

For paired-end data, use the following command: soap -a <Reads1.fastq> -b <Reads2.fastq> -d <Reference.fasta> -o <PEalignment.soap> -2 <SEalignment.soap> -p <# of parallel processes> -c 52 -s 12 -m <maximum insert size> -x <minimum insert size>
Sort the alignment results from each lane by chromosome names and then by mapping coordinates on each chromosome.
Merge sorted alignment results from all lanes into a single file, ensuring alignments remain sorted.
Split the merged alignments into separate files for each chromosome.
Download flat ASN files of dbSNP2 database and allele frequency information such as HapMap3 data for human resequencing.
Transform dbSNP information of each chromosome into a tab-delimited plain text file named "chrN.dbSNP.txt".
Build consensus sequence for each chromosome by SoapSNP using the command line:
Invoke SoapSNP with input alignment file, reference fasta file, output consensus file, and other parameters as required.
Extract potential SNP sites from each consensus file where called genotypes differ from reference genotypes and reference genotypes are not "N".
Record the distance to neighboring potential SNPs for each potential SNP site.
Filter raw SNP dataset to retain confident SNPs with quality scores larger than 20.
Ensure each allele is supported by more than a certain number of reads, depending on average sequencing depth (typically 2 for 20X data).
Maintain overall depth less than the average plus three times the standard deviation of sequencing depth.
Check that the average copy number of nearby regions around SNPs is less than 2.
Ensure each allele is supported by at least one paired-end read.
Verify SNP sites are at least 5bp away from another SNP.

Align all paired-end reads to reference genome using SOAP in gap alignment mode: soap -a <Reads1.fastq> -b <Reads2.fastq> -d <Reference.fasta> -o <PEalignment.soap> -2 <SEalignment.soap> -p <# of parallel processes> -c 52 -s 12 -m <maximum insert size> -x <minimum insert size> -g 3 -e 5.
Extract all gapped alignments from SOAP result and merge them into a single file.
Sort all gapped alignments by chromosome names lexicographically, followed by coordinates on each chromosome.
Extract coordinates, sizes, and numbers of supporting reads of potential indels from the alignments.
Select only one representative indel according to their number of supporting reads in each 10bp window.
Filter all potential indels to get confident ones that satisfy: a) supported by at least 3 reads; b) number of ungapped alignment crossing the indels no more than twice that of gapped reads.
Extract all abnormally aligned paired-end reads with unexpected orientations and/or span size.
Cluster abnormally aligned paired-end reads that have same alignment orientation and similar coordinates on both ends of read pairs.
Fit all abnormal paired-end clusters into alignment models and call potential structural variations (SVs).
Merge redundant called SVs.
Filter potential structural variations to get confident ones which satisfy the criteria.
Ensure each of the paired-end clusters supporting the SV comprises at least 4 read pairs.
Merge SVs that conflict with one another into complex structural variation cases.
